predictions.selection_reason: observable input/state -> construct security-sensitive value -> extracts externally controlled jsModuleId from FlashVars and uses it for module loading
predictions.source_summary: The jsModuleId value originates from FlashVars parameters passed to the SWF object by the hosting web page. These parameters are accessible through LoaderInfo.parameters and can be controlled by an attacker if the SWF is embedded with user-controllable flashvars.
predictions.sink_summary: The jsModuleId value, when present and of type string, is used in a security-sensitive ExternalInterface.call to JS_MODULE_WRAPPED_DISPATCHER. This dispatcher function uses require(jsModuleId) which can lead to arbitrary code execution if the jsModuleId points to a malicious module path.
predictions.guard_summary: There are no validation or sanitization controls on the jsModuleId value before it is used in the ExternalInterface.call. The only check is whether flashvars.jsModuleId exists and is a string, but no further restrictions are applied to prevent malicious values.
predictions.risk_pattern: An attacker can inject a malicious module ID through the jsModuleId FlashVar parameter, which will be passed directly to require() in the JS_MODULE_WRAPPED_DISPATCHER function, leading to potential arbitrary code execution.
predictions.context_summary: The ZeroClipboard SWF reads flashvars parameters to configure its behavior. When jsModuleId is provided and is a string, it's stored in a private variable and later used in a security-sensitive ExternalInterface.call that invokes require() with the attacker-controlled module ID.

retrieval_query.missing_control: No validation of module path before dynamic require
